title: Overrides as bounds, with an audit trail

questions.heading: An Override Is a Request, Checked Against the Data Before Any Bound Moves
questions.stem: override_trail.py sends planner-a's request 'P038 start_in 2029', and check() refuses it. What reason did the program print under entry #4?

options.text: P038 cannot start in 2029: its window is 2030-2031
options.says: Entry #4 printed 'P038 cannot start in 2029: its window is 2027-2027'.

options.text: P038 cannot start in 2029: its window is 2027-2027
options.says: Right: entry #4 printed 'P038 cannot start in 2029: its window is 2027-2027', and the request changed no bound.

options.text: P038 cannot start in 2029: its window is 2027-2028
options.says: P038's window is the single year 2027: entry #4 printed 'its window is 2027-2027'.

options.text: P038 cannot start in 2029: its window is 2030-2030
options.says: Entry #4 printed 'P038 cannot start in 2029: its window is 2027-2027'.

questions.heading: The Trail Records Who, When, Why and the Bounds That Moved, and Is Only Ever Appended To
questions.stem: At 09:10 a planner sets 'start_in 2029' on project P-7, whose window is 2028 to 2030. At 09:40 the same planner sets 'start_in 2030' on P-7. What does the trail hold for P-7 afterwards?

options.text: The 09:40 entry alone, since the trail keeps one entry per project
options.says: Entry 1 is not edited or deleted; it stays, because it was true at 09:10.

options.text: Both entries, the 09:40 one listing the three start variables of P-7
options.says: An entry lists only variables whose bounds moved; 2028 stays at (0, 0) and is not listed.

options.text: The 09:10 entry alone, since the 09:40 request is refused as a repeat
options.says: A new override on the same project supersedes the old one; it is not refused.

options.text: Both entries, the 09:40 one listing the two start variables that moved
options.says: Right: the trail is append-only, and entry 7 lists only 2029 and 2030.

questions.heading: When Overrides Make a Scenario Infeasible, the Trail Finds Which Ones
questions.stem: Four overrides make a scenario infeasible; without any override it solves. Dropping the newest leaves it infeasible, while dropping any one of the other three makes it solvable. What does the deletion filter over the trail report?

options.text: The three older overrides, with the planners who set them and why
options.says: Right: the newest stays dropped; each of the three is needed, so each is kept with its entry.

options.text: All four overrides, with the planners who set them and why
options.says: The filter keeps only overrides whose removal makes the scenario solvable; P021's outage window was dropped.

options.text: The newest override alone, with the planner who set it and why
options.says: Dropping the newest left the scenario infeasible, so it stays dropped and is not reported.

options.text: The newest and one older override, as the pair that conflicts
options.says: Each of the other three was needed for the conflict; the newest was not.
